intro.title: What does Exyconn build for healthcare providers?
intro.definition: is a set of administrative agents that handle appointments, routine patient questions, intake paperwork, report delivery and insurance documents, so reception and billing staff can look after the patients in the room. Exyconn designs, builds and runs these agents on top of your HMS or clinic software, WhatsApp Business account and phone line. They never diagnose, prescribe or triage on their own: anything clinical goes to a doctor or nurse.

benefits.title: Why clinics are doing this now

items.text: Patients who can't get through on the phone book with another clinic instead.
Every missed appointment is a slot a doctor could have used for someone else.
Paper forms filled in the waiting room mean retyping, errors and longer queues.
ABHA-linked records and digital claims are becoming the normal way of working in India.
Front-desk and billing teams are stretched, and repetitive work is what burns them out.

props.label: The reality
props.title: Where a clinic's hours actually go
props.lede: Ask a practice manager what fills the day and most of it happens away from the consulting room.

items.title: A phone that never stops
items.text: Booking, rescheduling, "is the doctor in today?" and directions all come by phone, while the same receptionist is checking in a queue of patients.

items.title: Empty slots from no-shows
items.text: Patients forget, or cancel without telling anyone. The slot sits empty while someone else was told there was nothing free until next week.

items.title: Paper forms and retyping
items.text: Histories, consent forms and insurance details are filled in by hand at the desk, then typed into the HMS, and copied again for the next visit.

items.title: "Are my reports ready?"
items.text: Lab and imaging reports bring a wave of calls and walk-ins. Abnormal results need a doctor's eye, and follow-up visits slip when nobody chases them.

items.title: Insurance paperwork that stalls
items.text: Cashless pre-authorisation and claims need the right documents for each TPA or insurer. A missing discharge summary or bill break-up sends the file back.

items.title: No clear view of the practice
items.text: Which doctor is overbooked, which slots go empty and how much is stuck in pending claims sits across the HMS, the billing desk and a few spreadsheets.

offerings.title: Six administrative jobs AI takes off your front desk

items.title: Appointment booking and reminders
items.text: Books, moves and cancels appointments against doctors' live schedules in your HMS, sends reminders with preparation notes, and offers freed slots to patients on the waitlist.

items.title: Patient queries on WhatsApp and phone
items.text: Answers timings, fees, directions, accepted insurers and visit preparation from your approved information. Symptoms and medical questions go straight to clinical staff, and emergencies are told to call emergency services.

items.title: Intake forms and records, digitised
items.text: Sends history, consent and insurance forms before the visit, reads uploaded prescriptions and ID documents, and files the details into the patient's record in the HMS for staff to verify.

items.title: Lab reports and follow-ups
items.text: Sends reports to patients once the lab or doctor releases them, routes results the doctor wants to discuss into a callback, and reminds patients when a follow-up or repeat test is due.

items.title: Billing and insurance claims
items.text: Builds the bill from the HMS, collects payment by UPI or card link, and assembles the document set for cashless pre-authorisation and claims to each TPA or insurer, with a billing executive submitting.

items.title: Clinic analytics
items.text: Reports footfall, no-shows, doctor utilisation, revenue by department and pending claims each morning, and answers questions like "which slots go empty most?" in plain language.

props.label: A day with it running
props.title: One day at a three-branch polyclinic
props.lede: A Monday at a polyclinic with general medicine, paediatrics and an in-house lab. Each moment lights the part of the clinic the agent is working on.

moments.title: Forms done before the doors open
moments.text: Patients booked for the morning have already filled in their history and consent forms on WhatsApp. The receptionist only has to check the flagged ones.

moments.title: The morning numbers
moments.text: The practice manager sees today's bookings by doctor, Friday's no-shows and the claims still waiting on a TPA, and moves a paediatrician to the busier branch.

moments.title: A cancellation, refilled
moments.text: A patient cancels a 12:00 slot by replying to her reminder. The agent offers it to the waitlist and a father with a feverish child takes it within minutes.

moments.title: A cashless file, complete
moments.text: For a day-care procedure, the agent gathers the ID, policy card, doctor's notes and estimate into the pre-authorisation set. The billing executive checks it and submits to the TPA.

moments.title: Reports out, one held back
moments.text: Forty blood reports are released and sent. One the doctor marked for discussion goes out as a callback request instead, booked for tomorrow morning.

moments.title: An evening question
moments.text: A parent asks if the clinic is open on Sunday and whether vaccinations need an appointment. The agent answers and books the slot; a question about side effects goes to the nurse's morning queue.

props.label: FAQ
props.title: Questions clinics and hospitals ask us

items.question: Does the AI give medical advice or triage patients?
items.answer: No. It handles administration only. Questions about symptoms, medicines or results go to your doctors or nurses, and anyone describing an emergency is told to call emergency services or come to the hospital straight away. Doctors decide what the agent is allowed to say.

items.question: Will it replace our receptionists?
items.answer: No. It takes the phone and WhatsApp load off the desk so receptionists can look after patients standing in front of them, and passes anything sensitive or unusual to them with the conversation attached.

items.question: Which HMS and lab systems can it work with?
items.answer: Any HMS, EMR or LIS with an API or a dependable export. Where your software is ABDM-enabled, the agent can work with ABHA-linked records through it. We confirm exactly what your systems allow in the first week.

items.question: How is patient data protected?
items.answer: Health data stays in your systems and a private environment we set up for you, with role-based access, encryption and a full audit log. Patients consent before we message them, and the setup follows the law that applies to you: India's DPDP Act and ABDM's rules, the GDPR in Europe or HIPAA in the United States.

items.question: Can patients use their own language?
items.answer: Yes. The agent works in English, Hindi and other Indian languages on WhatsApp and phone, while the approved answers are written once by your team.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: It depends on the number of doctors, branches and systems involved. Most clinics start with appointments and reminders; tell us about your practice and we'll send a fixed quote for that first phase.
